decision.state: Relevant organization-specific study; no program-level marginal estimate
decision.summary: Institute on Aging operates more than 20 aging and disability programs across distinct service and payment models, including the Friendship Line, community-living case management, dementia support, adult day services, and private-pay home care. A six-month, single-group Friendship Line pilot found favorable changes among 121 health-plan members, while a separate convenience-sample study found high satisfaction but persistent loneliness among frequent callers. Neither study estimates the program's causal effect. Broader reviews find uncertain case-management effects and very low-certainty friendly-visiting evidence. The organization therefore has plausible pathways and unusually relevant program-specific research, but no defensible organization-level impact price or current marginal funding estimate.

financialContext.period: FY2025 IRS EO BMF and organization financial statement; active SF prime-contract ledger as of 2026-08-20
financialContext.summary: The IRS California EO BMF and IOA's FY2025 financial statement both report $100.03 million in revenue; the statement also reports $96.91 million in expenses, $29.47 million in contributions, $69.71 million in program-service revenue, and $12.87 million in net assets. The city's ledger contains ten active prime contracts spanning Community Living Fund, case management, clinical collaboration, resource centers, adult day and dementia services, suicide prevention, and outreach.
financialContext.boundary: Organization finances combine charitable, contracted, program-service, and potentially private-pay activities across multiple geographies and programs. Contract award authority, payments, outstanding purchase orders, and remaining authority are different accounting fields, not interchangeable funding gaps. None identifies incremental philanthropic cost, the counterfactual use of restricted or unrestricted gifts, duplicated participants, payer displacement, or current capacity for a named program.

evidence.design: Organization-reported current program and reach description
evidence.population: Older adults, adults with disabilities, and caregivers across San Francisco, other Bay Area counties, and California
evidence.result: IOA describes more than 20 integrated programs and says its services touch more than 67,000 people annually. The Friendship Line reports more than 11,000 inbound and outbound calls each month, while the San Francisco Community Living Fund provides intensive case management to people leaving or at imminent risk of institutional care.
evidence.transfer: Portfolio reach, calls, referrals, assessments, and services use different units and may include repeat contacts. They do not establish unique people served, program completion, safe community tenure, reduced loneliness, avoided institutionalization, suicide prevention, or causal impact.

evidence.population: 121 older adults identified as at risk for loneliness through a Medicare Advantage health plan and offered proactive outbound Friendship Line calls
evidence.result: The share reporting loneliness fell from 46% to 28%; anxiety fell from 63% to 43%; depression changed from 36% to 25% without meeting the conventional statistical-significance threshold; unhealthy mental-health and physical-health days also declined.
evidence.transfer: The pilot had no concurrent control group, assignment was not randomized, participation and follow-up can select respondents, and pandemic-era trends or regression to the mean could explain part of the change. It supports feasibility and measurement, not the causal effect, unit cost, or current marginal value of Friendship Line calls.

evidence.population: 63 Friendship Line callers recruited by convenience sampling during 2020–2021, with 23 purposively sampled for qualitative interviews
evidence.result: Daily callers were more likely than non-daily callers to meet the study's chronic-loneliness definition (61% versus 18%) and reported high satisfaction and meaningful relationships with the line; the study documented distinct uses for chronic versus acute social needs.
evidence.transfer: Call frequency was self-selected rather than assigned, baseline need differed sharply, the sample was small, and there was no non-caller comparison. Satisfaction and perceived support are important user evidence but do not establish reduced loneliness, avoided emergency visits, suicide prevention, or cost-effectiveness.

evidence.population: 11,860 community-dwelling adults aged 65 or older living with frailty in high-income countries
evidence.result: Compared with usual care, case management may make little or no difference to mortality, nursing-home residence, quality of life, serious adverse effects, or physical function and probably makes little or no difference to hospital admission or costs; certainty was low to moderate.
evidence.transfer: This is transferable evidence for a broad intervention class, not IOA's Community Living Fund or other programs. Included models, teams, eligibility rules, usual care, and outcomes varied, and the review cannot supply IOA's local counterfactual effect or marginal cost.

evidence.design: 2023 Campbell systematic review of nine randomized and four non-randomized studies
evidence.population: 470 adults aged 60 or older, mostly in small six- to twelve-week face-to-face volunteer visiting programs
evidence.result: The review found very low-certainty evidence and could not determine whether volunteer friendly visiting reduces loneliness, social isolation, or related wellbeing outcomes in the short or intermediate term; no study reported long-term loneliness.
evidence.transfer: Face-to-face friendly visiting is not the same as IOA's multilingual 24/7 warm line, crisis support, or scheduled outbound calls. The review clarifies the weakness of the broader befriending evidence base but does not estimate the Friendship Line's effect.

model.nativeOutcome: an additional eligible older adult or adult with disabilities achieving a pre-specified sustained community-living, loneliness, mental-health, caregiver, dementia, safety, or access outcome because of one defined IOA program
missingInputs: One named IOA legal entity, program, geography, payer, eligible cohort, referral pathway, intervention dose, and intended durable outcome for the proposed gift
Complete participant flow from eligibility and referral through enrollment, service receipt, repeat contacts, completion, discharge, cross-program duplication, and follow-up

One pre-specified program-specific outcome with a meaningful threshold and duration, keeping community tenure, loneliness, mental health, caregiver outcomes, dementia support, safety, and access separate
Outcome reporting for all eligible participants including baseline severity, missing data, attrition, deaths, institutionalization, adverse events, subgroup results, and unsuccessful cases

A credible comparison for the selected program or a transparent, sensitivity-tested transfer from a sufficiently matched telephone-support, case-management, home-care, dementia, or adult-day evaluation
Incremental staff, volunteer, clinical, facility, technology, outreach, partner, and follow-up costs for the selected program and outcome window

Reconciliation of city contracts, Medicare or Medi-Cal payments, private-pay and program-service revenue, restricted contributions, partner services, displacement, and the counterfactual pathway without the gift
Time-bounded $100K, $1M, and $10M marginal plans with incremental participants, activities, capacity constraints, milestones, downside cases, and stop rules
model.qalyBoundary: MFI publishes a very-low-confidence estimate of approximately $14.9 million per 10 QALYs. It combines the judgmental 7% causal six-month remission probability with a 0.04 observational annual lonely-versus-not-lonely utility gap, 50% utility-gap retention, and 0.5-year effective duration. This is not a measured IOA effect or funding recommendation; null, harm, and displacement have no finite positive impact price.

reservations: IOA is a large multi-program organization; a portfolio total cannot be divided by calls, participants, or favorable outcomes to create a causal unit cost.
The 67,000-person reach figure does not publish counting rules, program mix, repeat-contact treatment, geography, or outcome follow-up.
Friendship Line call volume is not a unique-caller denominator, completed intervention, reduced-loneliness outcome, resolved crisis, or life saved.
The 121-person proactive-call study has no concurrent control group, so favorable within-participant changes cannot be assigned to the program alone.
The 63-caller observational study shows high need and perceived support but cannot compare calling more often with an assigned alternative.
Broader case-management and friendly-visiting evidence is heterogeneous and does not establish IOA's organization-specific effect.
FY2025 finances and ten multiyear city contracts do not identify private-gift additionality, payer displacement, program-level costs, or current capacity.
Without one bounded marginal plan, unrestricted support may be valuable but cannot receive a defensible outcome forecast or donor allocation.
